questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to experience the univeristy culture in the UK, especially with the many student networks and societies they have.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it has been quite easy to find the information that I needed, and I always knew who to get in touch with if I had questions related to either study or accomondation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I haven't reveived any assitance at my arrival but I had a check in with my student advisor during the semester which was really helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to receive an offer to stay in a uni accomondation. Options weren't really a thing because I wasn't guaranteed housing on campus since I was only in Edinburgh for a semester. I did make a list of priorities but unfortunately didn't get any of them. I then signed up to the uni's waitlist of spare rooms and got my offer about 1,5 week before my exchange started

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared flat with a shared kitchen as well. I was fortunate that previous students had left cutlery and ktichen utilities for us to use.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to find uni accomondation and you might end up with an offer that was not on your priority list and a bit more expensive than expected. However, I was really happy that I accepted the offer and had the whole housing situation sorted before my exchange. Typically most people get an offer, but I also met people who only got an offer after they arrived, so you have to be patient and trust the proces (or look for private accomondation)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I had to schedule an appointment for international check in and drop by the visiting student office to check in there as well. The registration was pretty easy, you just have to be aware that there are to separate check ins.
With the courses I just applied for them online and it was really easy to make changes to your course list too.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always ask your visiting student advisor and they usually get back to you very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the description of the courses and the type of exam they have too. Personally, I had three courses that were all year 3 or 4, and while I was for the most part happy with my courses, it would have been nice to have a course with a bit lower expectations/work load. Maybe just consider the balance between study work load and activities you want to do in your free time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two year 3 couses and one year 4 course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the style of teaching was more enganging and based on discussions, epecially the tutorials. It was very rare that the teachers would run through an article but instead they would situate the theories within a broader context and use the articles to facilitate a discussion on a certain topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took 'Culture and Power,' 'Spectacles and Crowds: anthropology through publics' and 'The Internet and Society.'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think spectacles and crowds was my favorite course because it was really engaging and very interesting theories. We had group presentations every week, which on one hand was a lot but on the other the amount of reading was less compared to my other courses which was really nice. I think culture and power was interesting too as it deals with extremely relevant political issues.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really encounter unexpected costs, but when I moved in I had to buy a few new things which added up in the end.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and going to cafés is less expensive than in Denmark I would say, and housing was definetly more expensive than I thought it would be!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different things. You can play a variety of sports through the uni's sports union, there are a lot of societies and networks to be a part of as well and they host almost weekly socials for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried a few different societies' events and joined the mountaineering clubs' weekly bouldering session which was super fun and a good way of meeting new people. I also went on an erasmus week-end trip to Isle of Skye which I totally would recommend. The nature was so beautiful and I met some really sweet people on the trip.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would reccommend to go on a trip to the highlands or just explore the many cute areas of the city. I went a few places, but think the best were Glenfinnan (the Harry Potter bridge:)) and Isle of Skye were my favorite. In Edinburgh, I can recommend Stockbridge, Portobello beach, Leith and ofc Old Town!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think the cultural differences were that challenging, but I find it really inspiring how Scotland has preserved a strong cultural identity.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were always very open and kind which I love

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Firstly, I think the university of Edinburgh has a lot of interesting courses and really good teachers who focus on engaging the students. Seconldy, the semester is quite short and the university's exam period is a bit more pressed than back home, so try to prioritize your studying and don't be afraid to reach out to your student advisor. Thirdly, the teaching style might be different from what you are used to, but I really enjoyed the opportunity of learing and studying in a another way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it is important to consider your courses and the level of them well. I chose a course outside my field and the course itself ended up being very confusing. If I were to do this again, I think I would choose maybe just one course that seemed a little 'easier' to give more room for fun activities and other things beside uni stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I would say meeting new people and other international students. Sharing such a big experience and making a lot of memories together just makes a really special bond which I am very grateful for.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably having time to do all of the things that I wanted to. I think uni can easily take up a lot of time but that it is also so important to connect with new people and try new things while being abroad!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
